body: Unawatuna Beach is a beautiful tropical paradise known for its golden sand, calm turquoise waters, and relaxed atmosphere. Palm trees provide natural shade, making it an ideal spot to unwind and soak in the scenery. The clear water and gentle waves make it safe for families and casual swimmers. body: The beautiful name of this village and beach is legendary from an Indian merchant who was shipwrecked and settled here. Unawatuna's one-kilometre beach stretched out in an arc. Its main advantage is the absence of a strong wave due to the double reef, which takes the shock load. The beach is good and profile. A gentle descent allows you to swim here with children, as well as people who are unable or poorly swim. That's probably why Unawatuna is popular with the local population, not just the Russians. Although the percentage of Sri Lankans able to swim seemed substantially higher than in India... However, the depths start at 10 or 15 meters. Another advantage of the beach is the availability of sunbeds. They're on display outside beach hotels and restaurants. You just have to grab drinks at the bar and use them all you want. Very convenient and cheap... We're into the Blue bistro restaurant. Unawatuna is not yet imbued with the spirit of commerce like other resorts, so pressing with extras like boats, bananas, parasailing and so on is practically non-existent. That's a plus to me. You can swim safely... The central part of the beach is more interesting, although most of the vacationers are for some reason in the northern part, although there is not far from the river flow. Not very good smelling, by the way... Maybe it's because there's a lot of restaurants and a few hotels. One last thing. Apart from its main purpose, Unawatuna Beach is good with sunsets. They won't leave even emotionally restrained people indifferent. It's best to see here...
title: Beautiful beach in every way.

body: Gorgeous beach, underdeveloped but with cafes close by. Not too many beach hassles. Sea quite wavy but lovely to swim in. Two things spoilt it. Very hard to prove except a) why only notice several minutes later? b) why did they not chase after us when we left? I cannot be sure but I think they were trying it on.When leaving we booked a cab with pickme, a hailing app which gets you the fair price not the tourist price. A tuktuk driver, looking for a customer, told us that pickme would not come here. I pointed out that we had come this way. He said it was drop off only. This seems a little odd. When our ride did arrive, driver was accosted aggressively and told he wasn't allowed to be in that area. The guy hit the outside of the car violently with us and children inside. It looks like this is a place with some kind of syndicate going on with some dishonest restaurants to boot. I might suggest giving this place a miss if you don't want to be caught up in that nonsense.

body: It's a lovely beach and was reminiscent of our many visits to Goa. Very chill with lots of possibilities to eat on the beach at night. Great sea food. Inexpensive places to stay . body: I circumnavigated Sri Lanka in three weeks. So as I headed to the coast from Ella, my first stop was Matara. From there to Mirissa and then onto Unawatuna. Locals try and trick you with over inflated prices. I liked Skinny Toms Delhi for food. My guesthouse was poor and just the general vibe I didn’t like. body: Unawatuna Beach is truly a slice of paradise on Sri Lanka’s southern coast! The soft golden sands, fringed by lush palm trees, create a stunning backdrop for relaxation and adventure.The water here is calm and ideal for swimming, making it perfect for families, including those with kids. The clear turquoise waters are also great for snorkeling, offering glimpses of vibrant marine life just a short swim from the shore.The beach vibe is lively yet serene, with plenty of cozy cafes and beachfront restaurants offering delicious local and international cuisine. Watching the sunset from Unawatuna Beach is a magical experience—don’t miss it!For the more adventurous, activities like paddleboarding and diving are available, and the friendly locals make the entire experience even more enjoyable.The cleanliness and maintenance of the beach stood out, and it’s well-managed, ensuring a safe and pleasant visit. Whether you’re looking to lounge in the sun, explore the underwater world, or enjoy a quiet moment by the sea, Unawatuna Beach has something for everyone.It’s a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Sri Lanka!
title: Unawatuna Beach: A Perfect Blend of Relaxation and Adventure!

body: I’m not quite sure what I was expecting at Unawatuna, I’ve read different reviews varying from describing it as a tropical paradise to a tourists hell hole. Either way, it was an incredible disappointment. As my Tuk Tuk meandered its way along the narrow Main Street, all my fears were realised, however it depends what you are looking for. If you want a lively beach front resort that is rammed with tourists, all I might point out, Russian (no problem there depending on your politics), with endless tacky shops and bars and a busy beach, this is your place. You will only hear Russian spoken, all the signs and menus are in Russian which isn’t anything to particularly detract from the experience, everyone is very well behaved, it’s just a bit overwhelming. There is a tower block sized hotel that caters solely to this market and floods the town in the evening. I had a little hotel on the outskirts of the town so didn’t have to deal with the very loud bars and restaurants nearer the centre which might be problematic to some people.My main concern was the pollution. Whilst the main town beach is fairly clean, the beaches at the Dutch watering hole and Jungle beach, are less clean unfortunately. Both beaches have precarious paths to them that are not for the faint hearted, on either beach there are sun beds for a minimal amount and a restaurant. The disheartening thing is that the paths to both beaches is strewn with rubbish, piles and piles of it. I really don’t understand why someone doesn’t organise a clean up, it’s absolutely filthy.The beach and sea at DWP is cleaner than at Jungle Beach which has a lot of rubbish floating in the sea. Not my idea of fun.Having booked to stay a week, my initial horror died down a bit on the second day and because my hotel was quiet and clean decided to,use the place as a base for scootering around but only for 5 days. Hopefully I’ll find some less hectic places down the coast which, if I return will be preferable to Sri Lanka’s answer to certain resorts in Majorca but then again, it’s snowing at home and 30 degrees here….
title: A great disappointment.

body: Admittedly, there are dirtier and uglier beaches on this planet (not to say it’s anything other than bang average). Filled with dodgy locals offering you everything from magic mushrooms to photos with baby monkeys on leashes that they stole from the jungle. body: The beach itself is good with plenty of options for sun beds, drinks and food. However I can't give 5* to this due to its VISITORS! Summing up the facts: this place is starting to look more like Russia than anything else. Many restaurants have the menu in Sinhalese and Russian with hidden English menus (in some, you even have to ask for it). I wouldn't mind that if it wasn't for the fact that tourists from this specific country are ruining the island. Of course there is good people and bad people everywhere, but I haven't seen other foreigners (from other countries) doing any of the following things: throwing rocks at dogs and laughing, removing corals from the sea into the land or throwing empty bottles of alcohol into the ocean. The behavior of these tourists is just unacceptable. Instead of seeing locals defending their area, we see them supporting this type of stuff/behavior. It's very sad to see this. We know Sri Lanka is in desperate need of tourism, but this type of tourism will destroy beautiful places. They get drunk and ruin your experience with their drunkenness. I hope the police starts patrolling the beach and making tourists have some respect for the public areas. They also have locals with wild caught monkeys on a leash passing by for pictures on top of you. Animal abuse, bad behavior and habitat destruction to say the least.
title: Good beach but bad tourists

body: I thought long and hard about if I should stay at Unawatuna beach and thought I would give it a shot. It ended up been the worst beach I stayed at on my trip. We spend one afternoon on it then went to Angel Beach club which is a 7 min tuk tuk drive. Highly recommend Angel as it’s on a nice beach and has a nice pool with good food and drink, don’t waste your time with Unawatuna
title: Worst beach we went to

body: If you are spending your hard earned money to go on holiday, then do not come to this beach. The place is scruffy, its become a draw for the budget traveller who has little money to spend. Its got groups of people who will buy bottles of vodka from the liqueur store and then sit next to you and order 1 bottle of coke and six empty glasses and spend all night getting drunk. Ladies be aware of the rastsa beach boys, they will be all over you, and watch your drinks, as illegal substances are offered in the the twilight hours. Men be aware, that knives are hidden under the sand around some popular night spots, and if you query a bar bill, then you will be surrounded. The tuk tuks are a rip off, the sand has been imported and is full of broken shells and cigarette buts. Dogs roam freely, and are allowed in the restaurant areas while you are trying to eat your meal. There are so many better areas in Sri Lanka to holiday, give this place a miss.
title: Poor

body: Nice sandy beach in a bay with sometimes really big waves. Too bad the water is sometimes quite full of rubbish and the beach starts to be full of plastic dirt too. Diving and snorkeling boats cross with high speed the swimming zone and if you are in the way they'd rather whistle that you'd step out of way than slow down itself. A pity for this beautiful beach.
title: In danger of being destroyed by mass tourism

body: Any trip to Sri Lanka must include Unawatuna Beach. The restauarnts are really plentiful & good. The people are friendly & it's easy to get around with Tuk tuks in abundance. It's a short tuk tuk ride to Galle if you need a bit of sightseeing , history & shopping, but if relaxing is your plan then the beaches are perfect.
title: Great swimming beach with loads of good restaurants, cafes & shopping.

body: The town of Unawatuna has grown leaps and bounds over the years, the beach the economic driver. It is a nice, sandy beach in which you sink with every step. The stretch opposite my hotel was just for swimming and chilling. The waves were not a big issue. If you stand with your back to the water you have a string of resorts and restaurants. Fresh fish caught offshore can be on your plate every night though it is appreciably higher priced than your standard curry and rice fare. Dinner on the beach is a good experience. Could not get the hotel wifi to upload pix in any reasonable amount of time.
title: BEAUTIFUL SPOT

body: Somewhat unusually I've found that the last dozen reviews sum this place up pretty accuracy. The main beach is over developed but very pleasant. Many restaurants from the fantastic to mediocre. Beach safeish for kids (slopes away quickly with some undertow - don't leave them unsupervised). Plenty of Russians. Ok for a couple of days, but not the real Sri Lanka.

body: This picture postcard location has been over-exploited and literally trashed in some aspects. The basics are all still good, but are tarnished by uncontrolled development of hotels and bars, most shockingly in the case of the multi-storey monstrosity being built at the right hand side; unregulated and therefore extremely dangerous jetski and boat use in the swimming area; noise from beach parties into the early hours, and lack of regular cleaning up of litter and plastic washed up on the shore. All of these nuisances could be prevented and fixed so that the special charm of this lovely spot continues to attract holidaymakers and provide a living for the friendly and laid-back locals.

body: People go to beaches for different reasons. My ideal beach has no undertow or current and is deep enough to swim as if you are in a swimming pool. Unawatuna beach ticks those boxes.It is a bay protected by a reef that keeps the dangerous current of the Indian Ocean out. It is actually one of the few beaches in Sri Lanka where you can swim without getting drowned. The safest side is towards the temple. There the water is even suitable for small children. When you swim from the temple towards the main road you feel when the waves get stronger. There will be no undertow, but the waves will be too strong to swim pleasant swimming pool like laps. The downside of the Unawatuna beach is that all the boats are floating in the part that is most suitable for swimming! You will have to swim around these boats or worse inhale the petrol fumes! How can tourist enjoy the freshness of the sea air when the have to inhale stinking petrol!The beach is for Sri Lankan standards wide. Non swimming tourists like to enjoy this beach to lie in the sun or drink cocktails. This beach is however completely artificial. The municipality puts this sand which is different from real beach sand. The sea erodes this sand and then more sand needs to be put to keep the beach. The result is a smaller bay to swim and less clear water due to the eroding sand floating on the water!
title: Like a swimming pool but with petrol fumes

body: We are visiting out of season so we had practically the whole beach to ourselves. Lovely beach to walk along and to jump in the waves. Be careful though as there is a strong current in some places. The beach has beach bars and restaurants and I can see it being a hive of activity in the peak season months. We opted to have drinks and a snack at The Lucky Tuna and they allowed us to use their sunloungers for free. I would have given the beach a 5, but the number of people offering massages, surfing, diving, clothes, hair braiding, bracelets, sarongs, jewellery, coconuts and stories of the tsunami ..... well with the list of things offered you can see it was not relaxing. They were relentless with the same people asking time and time again. I am always polite, but did finally have to ask them to go away as I was not interested. I know they are desperate for sales, but pestering people deters them...well in my case it does. Beautiful beach though and we enjoyed our day.
title: Pretty Beach

I sat in one cafe and had a beer and a shisha whilst petting a local stray dog for an hour, a very wholesome experience.

body: We went to Unawatuna twice during our holiday. The beach was disappearing with the Monsoon season starting and in some spots the loungers were teetering on the edge of a drop! There are lots of lounge areas with prices ranging hugely in price, from a very basic 100slr through to 2500slr but this comes with cool water spritzing, extremely comfortable lounge areas and attentive service. There are safe flagged areas to swim and you can go out to the reef on a glass bottom boat (for a price) there are a few sellers but they are not pushy and will move on with a gentle no thank you! Lots of restaurants and bars along the beach

body: Unfortunately just like most other beautiful places, it is polluted with plastic bags and waste from near by establishments. In addition to pollution the beach is over crowded . The road to the beach is narrow and not carpeted properly. Surprisingly the water did look blue and clear despite having a stream polluted water meet the sea near the bathing area.On the bright side, the shallow water reduces the risk of drowning, so it's a safe place for the entire family to bathe (even toddlers) Also the area is safe as there are many tourists and locals.There were some boats offering short sea tours for LKR 1500 (10 min) and LKR 2500 (20 min) we paid LKR 200 for parking the car for about 2 hr and LKR to shower after bathing in the sea

body: After travelling around Sri Lanka for 2 weeks, it was lovely to finally get our toes into the sand and experience one of Sri Lanka’s lovely pristine beaches. Our teenage daughters very grateful to be finally at a beach and not seeing another Tea Leaf or Temple!!Sun lounges line the beach with umbrellas, so you can really set yourself up here to enjoy the whole day Beach front.Nice relaxed & chilled out cafes and beach restaurants couple of footsteps back from the beach.The whole area filled with back packers and a great mix of very interesting people from all walks of life!!We only came here for a few hours but this place definitely on our list of places to stay next visit to SL

title: Great beach with wonderful village behind it
body: Unawatuna beach is beautiful, clean sandy beach, clear water with prefect temperature (in January). There are dozens of shady bars and restaurants along the back of the beach where you can go for lunch and dinner (they move extra tables out onto the sand at night so you can dine on the beach at night). There is a narrow village street that runs from the beach up to the main road that has lots of restaurants, bars, shops etc, which for us was a highlight of the place. If you stay at Calamander Beach Resort they do not tell about this street and if you don’t know where it is, it is possible that you can stay at Unawatuna beach for a week and not even know that it is there, so make sure you find it! (You can walk through to the village street from some of the other hotels, such as Tartaruga Hotel & restaurant, you walk through the driveway, turn left and right along a few short laneways and then you pop out into the middle of the village!). We loved this village, there are good rooftop bars such as The hideout, and good restaurants such as the Happy Spice, which is down the lane way behind the Pink Elephant (another good restaurant), and the Shifting Sands.We stayed at Calamander Beach Resort and although our rooms were pretty good, the service was underwhelming, meals took far too long so the restaurants were not busy, and we think there were better (and probably better value) places to stay that are also on the beachfront or in/near the village, with a very short walk to the beach. We stayed in 6 different hotels in Sri Lanka and we rated Calamander as the lowest in terms of value for money and service. But we loved Unawatuna both as a beach and a village, thoroughly recommend staying there.

title: Best Sri Lankan Beach
body: Wide, white sand beach with clear waters. You can ride 20' on a wave runner for US$40. Para-gliding is also offered on the beach.
